hero.lede: Hold one share of the listed parent before the RHP date to apply in the shareholder category, a second shot at allotment on top of retail.

steps.title: Hold one share of the parent
steps.body: A single share of the listed parent is usually enough. The RHP sets the exact rule, so check it for each IPO.

steps.title: Have it in demat by the RHP date
steps.body: Eligibility is fixed on the date of the red herring prospectus, often about a week before the IPO opens. Buy at least a day before so the trade settles.

steps.title: Apply in the shareholder category
steps.body: Bid up to ₹2 lakh as a shareholder. You can still apply as retail or HNI too, and the two are not counted as multiple bids.

steps.title: A separate pool to be allotted from
steps.body: The quota, up to 10% of the issue, is allotted only among eligible shareholders. That pool is apart from retail, not instead of it.

items.q: What is a shareholder quota in an IPO?
items.a: When a listed company takes a subsidiary or group company public, the IPO can set aside up to 10% of the issue for the listed parent's shareholders. Only people who hold the parent's shares on the eligibility date can bid in that portion.

items.q: When do I need to own the parent's shares?
items.a: On the date of the red herring prospectus (RHP), or the record date the RHP names. The shares must be in your demat account by then, so a purchase on that day may be too late.

items.q: Can the shareholder quota be dropped?
items.a: Yes. A draft offer document (DRHP) can change before the final RHP, and a company that only announced an IPO has not committed to anything yet. That is why each IPO here shows its stage and a link to its offer document.
We check offer documents filed with SEBI, NSE and BSE every day for a shareholder reservation and the parent it names. IPOs drop off once they list, or when a SEBI approval lapses without dates.

card.buyByNote: Buy the parent by the last day shown below. Shares settle the next trading day, so a later purchase misses the record date.

stageNote.dates: The RHP is out, so the eligibility date may already have passed. Check the RHP before you buy the parent.
stageNote.approved: SEBI has cleared the draft. Dates usually follow within months. Hold the parent before the RHP date.
stageNote.filed: The draft offer document has a shareholder quota. It is waiting for SEBI's approval.
stageNote.announced: The quota comes from the company's announcement. There is no offer document yet, so it could still change.
